title: POST /api/internal/notifications with a valid X-Internal-Token dispatches and returns the created id
description: Simulates vendor-service/risk-management-service/trust-vault-service calling the internal notification endpoint to push a notification into the central bell without user auth.
preconditions: A valid targetUserId and organizationId exist
steps: POST /api/internal/notifications with header X-Internal-Token=<configured token> and body { targetUserId, organizationId, message: 'Vendor assessment overdue', notificationType: 'task_overdue', sourceModule: 'vendor' }
expectedResult: Response is 201 with { success: true, data: { id: <notificationId> } }, and a Notification document is persisted with sourceModule='vendor' and notificationType='task_overdue'.

title: POST /api/internal/notifications rejects requests missing targetUserId, organizationId, or message with 400
steps: POST /api/internal/notifications with a valid token but body missing 'message'
expectedResult: 400 response: { success: false, error: 'targetUserId, organizationId, and message are required' }. No document is created.

title: dispatch() enqueues a BullMQ 'deliver' job that the worker consumes and emits over Socket.IO
description: End-to-end of the documented pipeline: dispatch -> MongoDB -> BullMQ (notification-dispatch queue, job name 'deliver', payload { notificationId }) -> notification.worker.js fetches the doc and emits 'notification' to room org:{organizationId}:user:{targetUserId}.
preconditions: A test Socket.IO client is connected and joined to org:{orgId}:user:{userId}
steps: Call notificationService.dispatch({ targetUserId, organizationId, message: 'Audit invitation', notificationType: 'audit_invitation' })
Wait for the notification-dispatch queue to process the enqueued 'deliver' job
Observe events received by the connected test Socket.IO client
expectedResult: The client receives a 'notification' event whose payload includes _id, notificationType='audit_invitation', message='Audit invitation', isRead=false, matching the persisted document.

title: dispatch() falls back to a direct Socket.IO emit when BullMQ is unavailable
description: notification.service.js catches a queue.add() failure (Redis down / REDIS_ENABLED=false) and, when job is null, calls getIo() directly and emits 'notification' to the same org-scoped room, so delivery isn't silently lost even though the async worker path never ran.
preconditions: REDIS_ENABLED=false or Redis intentionally stopped for this test
A connected Socket.IO test client in the target user's room
steps: With Redis unavailable, call notificationService.dispatch({ targetUserId, organizationId, message: 'Fallback test' })
expectedResult: The client still receives the 'notification' event with the correct payload, delivered via the direct-emit fallback path rather than the BullMQ worker, and the Notification document is persisted regardless.

title: GET /api/notifications/client paginates correctly across multiple pages
expectedResult: Page 1 and 2 each return 20 notifications, page 3 returns 5. pagination.total=45, pagination.totalPages=3, and no notification appears on two different pages (stable sort by createdAt desc).

title: PUT /api/notifications/:id/read returns 404 for a notification owned by a different user
preconditions: Notification N belongs to User A
expectedResult: 404 'Notification not found' — N.isRead remains false in the database; no cross-user state mutation occurs.
requirement: OWASP API1 Broken Object Level Authorization

title: PUT /api/notifications/mark-all-read only flips isRead for the caller's own org + user scope
preconditions: User A (org X) has 4 unread notifications
User B (org X) has 2 unread notifications
User A also somehow has a stray notification with organizationId = org Y (data anomaly guard)
expectedResult: Response { modifiedCount: 4 } — only User A's org-X notifications flip to isRead=true; User B's 2 unread notifications and the org-Y stray notification are untouched.

title: join-project-room rejects a projectId belonging to a different organization than the authenticated socket
description: core/socket.js join-project-room handler looks up the Project by id and compares project.organizationId to socket.orgId (derived from the verified JWT during the io.use auth middleware, never from client input). Mismatch emits 'project-room-join-denied' and the socket never joins the room.
preconditions: Project P belongs to Org A
A valid JWT for a user in Org B
steps: Connect a Socket.IO client authenticated as an Org B user
expectedResult: The client receives 'project-room-join-denied' with { projectId: P._id } and is never added to room project:{P._id} — subsequent scan events for P are not delivered to this socket.

title: Redis pub/sub scan-progress message is relayed to the correct project Socket.IO room
description: The Python scan worker publishes to prowler-{environment}:scan:progress:{projectId}; core/socket.js psubscribes to that pattern, parses projectId from the payload or channel suffix, maps status→event name (running→scan-progress, completed→scan-completed, etc.) and emits to room project:{projectId} only.
preconditions: Two Socket.IO clients each joined to a different project's room (project:P1 and project:P2)
steps: Publish a message to prowler-{env}:scan:progress:P1 with { projectId: 'P1', scanId: 'SCAN-1', status: 'running', progress: 40 }
expectedResult: Only the client in room project:P1 receives a 'scan-progress' event with progress=40; the client in project:P2 receives nothing for this message.
